items.question: Do I need to know how to write AI video prompts?
items.answer: No. BearAi writes the entire script and every shot-level prompt for you, using accurate cinematography terminology. You only provide a topic or an image.

items.question: Which AI video tools do the prompts work with?
items.answer: The prompts are written in dense, comma-separated cinematic style compatible with Runway, Kling, Luma, Pika, Sora, Veo, and most other text-to-video generators.

items.question: Can I use a reference image instead of typing an idea?
items.answer: Yes. Switch to image mode, upload a reference photo, and BearAi analyzes it to infer a creative direction you can edit before generating.

items.question: Can I regenerate just one scene?
items.answer: Yes. Every scene card has a Regenerate button that re-runs only that scene while keeping the rest of your timeline untouched.

items.question: How long can my video be?
items.answer: Choose a target duration of 15, 30, 60, or 90 seconds — BearAi breaks it into the right number of 3–5 second scenes automatically.

about.title: We built BearAi so you never have to write an AI video prompt by hand.
about.intro: Writing a good AI video prompt means knowing screenwriting, shot composition, and cinematography vocabulary all at once. Most creators know what they want a clip to feel like — not the exact words a video model needs to hear. BearAi closes that gap.

pillars.title: Screenwriting, handled
pillars.description: BearAi reads your topic — or a reference image — and writes a short-form script built for how people actually watch video today.

pillars.title: Real direction, not guesswork
pillars.description: Every scene is staged with intentional camera movement, framing, angle, and lighting, drawn from a professional cinematography vocabulary.

pillars.title: One paste away from a clip
pillars.description: Prompts are dense, self-contained, and formatted the way generators like Runway, Kling, Luma, Pika, Sora, and Veo expect them.
